info.x-ibm-summary: API for the API Connect Analytics subsystem
info.description:
## API for the API Connect Analytics subsystem
This API includes the capability to retrieve information about API events stored in APIC Analytics,  retrieve the data used by the Analytics dashboards in the UI, obtain information on what filter parameters are supported  and also obtain information about internal cluster management, health and operations.
### API Events
There are operations to retrieve a count of events, a list of events or a specific detailed API event at the following  scopes: cloud, provider organization, catalog and space. The API event operations all support a multitude of filter parameters to be able to select the exact events you wish. These filter parameters can be combined together in a single query.
#### Data selection
There are advanced selectors available for these filter parameters too which allow operations such as these:
- `.../events?consumer_org_id=1234567890` = select all events made by consumer org id 1234567890
- `.../events?consumer_org_id=not:1234567890` = select all events made by consumer orgs other than id 1234567890
- `.../events?product_name=contains:loan` = select all events where the product name contained the string 'loan' (equivalent to searching for `*loan*`)
- `.../events?product_name=notcontains:loan` = select all events where the product name didn't contain the string 'loan'
- `.../events?product_name=startswith:loa` = select all events where the product name starts with the string 'loa' (equivalent to searching for `loa*`)
- `.../events?product_name=endswith:oan` = select all events where the product name ends with the string 'oan' (equivalent to searching for `*oan`)
- `.../events?product_name=regex:[a-z]oan` = select all events where the product name begins with any lowercase alphabetical character and ends with the string 'oan' (WARNING: Regex based queries have a performance impact and should only be used if other queries cannot be used)
- `.../events?product_name=isset` = select all events where the product_name field has a value that is not null and not an empty string
- `.../events?product_name=isnotset` = select all events where the product_name field is either null or an empty string
- `.../events?product_name=oneof:loans,accounts,address` = select all events where the product name is loans, accounts or address
- `.../events?product_name=oneof:loans\,accounts,address` = select all events where the product name is either 'loans,account' or 'address' ('\' escapes the first comma)
- `.../events?product_name=oneof:loans,accounts\,address` = select all events where the product name is either 'loans' or 'account,address' ('\' escapes the second comma)
- `.../events?product_name=notoneof:loans,accounts,address` = select all events where the product name is neither loans, accounts or address
- `.../events?product_name=notoneof:loans\,accounts,address` = select all events where the product name is neither 'loans,account' or 'address' ('\' escapes the first comma)
- `.../events?product_name=notoneof:loans,accounts\,address` = select all events where the product name is neither 'loans' or 'account,address' ('\' escapes the second comma)
- `.../events?product_name=equals:not:loan` = select all events where the product name is exactly 'not:loan'
- `.../events?product_name=not:not:loan` = select all events where the product name is not 'not:loan'
These ones only apply to numeric fields:
- `.../events?bytes_received=1000` = select all events where the received bytes was exactly 1000
- `.../events?bytes_received=gt:1000` = select all events where the received bytes was greater than 1000
- `.../events?bytes_received=gte:1000` = select all events where the received bytes was greater than or equals to 1000
- `.../events?bytes_received=lt:1000` = select all events where the received bytes was less than 1000
- `.../events?bytes_received=lte:1000` = select all events where the received bytes was less than or equals to 1000

The full list of possible advanced operator prefixes are: `not`, `contains`, `notcontains`, `startswith`, `endswith`, `regex`, `isset`, `isnotset`, `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `oneof`.

The exception to the above are the IP address fields `client_ip`, `gateway_ip` and `immediate_client_ip` which only support equality checks and `not` but none of the other operators. However, they do support CIDR based queries, for example:
- `.../events?client_ip=9.123.234.0/24` = select all events where the client IP address was in the 9.123.234.0 network (netmask 255.255.255.0)
#### Pagination
To control how many results are returned and navigate through pages of results use the standard `limit` and `offset` query parameters. The event list operations will return a maximum of 10,000 api events, to retrieve larger amounts of data use the scroll operations at cloud or organization scope.
#### Sorting
To sort the results based on the field names. By default, the sorting is in ascending order. To sort in descending order, prefix the field name with a -. Example: sort=api_name, sort=-product_name
#### Returning a subset of fields
The `fields` parameter can be used to only return a subset of fields in the api event records. Use a comma separated list of desired fields.
### Dashboards
These operations allow you to download the data used by the APIC Analytics dashboards in the API Manager UI.  These are also at the same variety of scopes and also support the same filter parameters as usable with the API Event operations above.
### Filter parameters
These operations define what filter parameters and operations are available at each scope.  This could be useful in a dynamically generated UI calling the API Event or dashboard operations above.
### Cluster Management
These operations allow the retrieval of information on cluster health and status as well as the ability to perform  maintenance operations on it.

/{analytics-service}/cloud/events.description: Return a result set of analytics API events scoped to the cloud. The items in the result set are determined by the passed in request query to this API. The order of the result set is sorted from newest to oldest events by specified 'datetime'.

get.summary: List events at cloud scope
get.description: Returns a result set of analytics API events scoped to the cloud. The items in the result set are determined by the passed in request query to this API. The order of the result set is sorted from newest to oldest events by specified 'datetime'. In this API, references to 'field' refer to the analytics API event fields documented here: https://www.ibm.com/docs/SSMNED_12.1.x_cd/com.ibm.apic.analytics.doc/api_event_records_fields.html Note this operation is limited to only being able to return 10,000 events, if you need more than that then use the scroll operation.

/{analytics-service}/cloud/events/scroll.description: You can use the scroll operation to retrieve a large number of results. You can request an unlimited number of results in batches.

post.summary: Scroll through results in batches
post.description: Returns an initial batch of results following the requested size or a default of 1000 as well as a 'scroll_id'. Pass this scroll ID to the next scroll operation to get back the next batch of results. Typically, the scroll ID does not change between requests, but it can change, so make sure to always use the latest scroll ID.

post.description: Clears the scroll search context and results for a scrolling search. Should be used when the scroll context is not needed since otherwise it will stay open until it times out.

/{analytics-service}/cloud/events/{event.description: Return investigation context for a single analytics API event scoped to the cloud: how the event compares with recent calls to the same operation, whether other calls around the same time had the same problem, what changed shortly before the event, and related calls.

get.summary: Get investigation context for an event at cloud scope
get.description: Return investigation context for a single analytics API event scoped to the cloud. The response has four optional sections, each omitted when it cannot be calculated. 'baseline' compares the event's latency, sizes and status code with the same operation over the previous 24 hours. 'blast_radius' gives call and error counts, per-minute, for 15 minutes either side of the event for the operation, API, backend, gateway service and application. 'changes' lists changes detected in the 24 hours before the event, from API event traffic (for example a new gateway version or a backend starting to fail), from product lifecycle updates received from API Manager and, when the caller has permission to view audit data and audit data is sent to analytics, from API Manager audit events for the event's API, product, application and consumer organization. 'performance' compares the event's assembly policy durations with recent successful calls to the same operation and gives hourly latency percentiles. 'related' lists calls that share the event's global transaction ID, calls from the same client within 60 seconds, and the trace ID. All date-time values are UTC.

1. Initial Request: Make your first API call with the desired parameters (timeframe, start/end dates, etc.)
2. 202 Response: If the report is not yet generated, you'll receive a 202 (Accepted) status with a message indicating the report is being generated

- Reports are cached based on the scope and time period parameters

timeframe_optional.name: timeframe

The key specifies the field to evaluate within the user agent object (e.g., `device`, `major`, `minor`, `name`, `os`, `os_full`, `os_major`, `os_minor`, `os_name`, `os_version`, `patch`, `version`).

verbose_optional.description: Whether to show all, or just basic snapshot information. If true, returns all information. If false, omits information like start/end times, failures, and shards. Optional, defaults to true.

voting_timeout_optional.name: timeout
voting_timeout_optional.description: Time to wait for the specified nodes to be excluded from the voting configuration before returning. Defaults to 30s.

wait_for_active_shards_optional.name: wait_for_active_shards
wait_for_active_shards_optional.description: A number controlling to how many active shards to wait for, all to wait for all shards in the cluster to be active, or 0 to not wait. Defaults to 0.

wait_for_events_optional.name: wait_for_events
wait_for_events_optional.description: Wait until all currently queued events with the given priority are processed.

wait_for_metadata_version_optional.name: wait_for_metadata_version
wait_for_metadata_version_optional.description: Waits for the metadata version to be equal or greater than the specified metadata version.

wait_for_no_initializing_shards_optional.name: wait_for_no_initializing_shards
wait_for_no_initializing_shards_optional.description: boolean value which controls whether to wait (until the timeout provided) for the cluster to have no shard initializations. Defaults to false, which means it will not wait for initializing shards.

wait_for_no_relocating_shards_optional.name: wait_for_no_relocating_shards
wait_for_no_relocating_shards_optional.description: A boolean value which controls whether to wait (until the timeout provided) for the cluster to have no shard relocations. Defaults to false, which means it will not wait for relocating shards.

wait_for_removal_optional.name: wait_for_removal
wait_for_removal_optional.description: Specifies whether to wait for all excluded nodes to be removed from the cluster before clearing the voting configuration exclusions list. Defaults to true.

wait_for_completion_optional.name: wait_for_completion
wait_for_completion_optional.description: Should the request block until the task is complete. Defaults to false.

wait_for_nodes_optional.name: wait_for_nodes
wait_for_nodes_optional.description: The request waits until the specified number N of nodes is available. It also accepts >=N, <=N, >N and <N. Alternatively, it is possible to use ge(N), le(N), gt(N) and lt(N) notation.

wait_for_status_optional.name: wait_for_status
wait_for_status_optional.description: Will wait (until the timeout provided) until the status of the cluster changes to the one provided or better, i.e. green > yellow > red. By default, will not wait for any status.

wait_for_timeout_optional.name: wait_for_timeout
wait_for_timeout_optional.description: Specifies the maximum time to wait for wait_for_metadata_version before timing out.

wait_if_ongoing_optional.name: wait_if_ongoing

scope_field.description: Event field the baseline is grouped on, for example api_resource_id.

period.description: Length of the baseline period, for example 24h.

lookback.description: How far back changes were looked for, for example 24h.
